title: Open Trivia
oneLiner: Multi-round trivia against the Open Trivia DB—scorekeeping, categories, and a clean game loop in the browser.

problem.heading: Problem
problem.description: Quiz demos often fetch one random batch and call it done. I wanted rounds, difficulty cues, and resilient handling when the public API throttles or returns edge-case payloads—without a custom backend.

myRole.heading: My role
myRole.description: Solo front-end build: game state machine for rounds and scoring, debounced fetches, loading and error UX, and layout that stayed readable on phones during timed questions.

solution.heading: Solution
solution.description: React app that composes Open Trivia API responses into a structured match flow—category pick, staggered reveals, running totals, and restart paths. Cached minimal client metadata so repeat plays did not hammer the API.

impact.heading: Impact
metrics: 🎮 Full game loop in the browser—no custom backend
🛟 Graceful handling when categories or API payloads came back empty
📖 Fork-friendly structure for demos and teaching
impact.description: A small product story: external API as the brain, disciplined UI as the differentiator.
